newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MICKELSON LEADS SPRINT INTERNATIONAL IN SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MICKELSON LEADS SPRINT INTERNATIONAL IN SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Phil Mickelson enhanced his prospects of nailing down a spot on the U.S. Ryder Cup team when he opened a handy lead after his second round at the $1.7 million Sprint International Friday.
Mickelson shot a five-under-par 67 on the saturated Castle Pines course, earning 13 points under the modified Stableford scoring system being used for the event.
He posted a halfway total of 27 points -- a tournament record low score for the first 36 holes -- to lead by four points over Larry Mize.

Skip Kendall and Neal Lancaster were five points back with 45 players still needing to complete their second rounds on Saturday. Best-placed among those was Scott McCarron, on 22 points with two holes left.
The scoring awards five points for eagle, two for birdie, zero for par, and subtracts one point for bogey and three points for double bogey or worse.
Mickelson reeled off three birdies and an eagle on the front nine, but struggled slightly coming home, adding two birdies and two bogeys on the back nine.
"I didn't play nearly as well on the back," said the 1993 champion. "Coming in I made a couple of blunders. I was a little disappointed."

Mickelson is ninth in the U.S. Ryder Cup standings and a top-10 finish here would greatly improve his chances of making the team, which will be finalised after the PGA Championship in two weeks. The top 10 players on the list qualify automatically.

Kendall, who has never finished better than seventh in a PGA Tour event, moved into the hunt for his best career result. He made four of his six birdies from inside six feet after some fine approach shots.
"I love this place. It seems to suit my game," said Kendall, who was forced to complete the first round early Friday following Thursday's weather delay.
"I had to play 32 holes today. That's a lot around here. It was very tiring. I tried to pace myself."
Zimbabwean Nick Price, on 20 points, was back on the right track after a strained left shoulder tendon forced him to withdraw from the Western Open four weeks ago.
A subsequent cortisone injection healed the injury, but he missed the cut at the British Open after taking a 78 in the windswept first round.
"The shoulder was fine, but I wasn't swinging very well," Price said. "The lack of continuity didn't help. The first round of the British Open was very difficult. I lost a bit of confidence."
Price regained a measure of confidence Friday as he reeled off seven birdies in a bogey-free 65.
"As the day progressed I got better and better," he said. "On the back nine I hit some pretty good iron shots."
